functionality: E-commerce Shopping and Order Management System

chunks.text: business objective: To develop an online shopping platform where customers can browse products, add items to their cart, make secure payments and track their orders. users and roles: Customers can browse and purchase products. Administrators can manage products, inventory and orders. Delivery personnel can update delivery status. workflow and outcomes: The application allows customers to browse products, search for items, add products to their shopping cart, and place orders. Customers can make online payments and track their orders. Administrators can manage products, update inventory, view customer orders, and handle cancellations.

The expected outcome is a smooth, secure, and user-friendly online shopping experience with efficient order management. business rules: Customers must register or log in before placing an order. Products can be added to the cart only if they are in stock. Orders should be confirmed only after successful payment. If payment fails, the order should not be placed. Customers can cancel orders before they are shipped, and administrators can update product prices and stock availability. exceptions: If a product becomes out of stock while a customer is placing an order, the system should notify the customer and prevent the purchase.

If payment fails or gets interrupted, the customer should be allowed to retry the payment. If an order is already shipped, cancellation may not be allowed. Administrators can override product availability and order status when necessary. data and integrations: The application stores customer details, product information, product prices, inventory, shopping cart items, orders, and payment details. It integrates with a payment gateway to process online transactions and a delivery service to track shipments. Customer and order information should be stored securely and updated whenever a purchase or order status changes.

security and compliance: The application should protect customer information such as personal details, passwords, and payment data. User authentication and role-based access should be provided to prevent unauthorised access. Payment transactions must be processed securely, and customer data should be protected during storage and transmission. The system should also provide secure order and transaction records. service levels and scale: The e-commerce application should support multiple customers browsing and purchasing products simultaneously. It should handle increasing numbers of products, orders, and users without affecting performance.

The system should remain available during peak shopping periods and process orders and payments efficiently. delivery constraints: The application will initially be developed as a web-based e-commerce platform accessible through desktop and mobile browsers. It should provide a simple and user-friendly interface for customers, administrators, and delivery personnel. The system will be developed in multiple stages, starting with product browsing, cart management, payment processing, and order tracking, followed by additional features based on user feedback.

validation and rollout: The application will be tested to ensure that product browsing, cart management, payment processing, and order tracking work correctly. Functional testing, usability testing, and security testing will be performed to identify errors. Initially, the application will be tested with a small group of users, and feedback will be collected to improve the system before its final deployment.

Clarification response for REQ-001: REQ-001: Has the security, privacy, and compliance applicability for this requirement been confirmed? Answer: "Yes. The requirement involves customer information, orders, and payments. Authentication, secure payment processing, and protection of customer data are applicable."

Clarification response for REQ-001: REQ-001: Has the security, privacy, and compliance applicability for this requirement been confirmed? Answer: "Yes. The requirement involves customer information, orders, and payments. Authentication, secure payment processing, and protection of customer data are applicable."

Clarification response for REQ-003: REQ-003: What measurable threshold or observable outcome should replace the qualitative wording? Answer: "Customers should be able to browse products and add items to their cart within three navigation steps. Administrators should be able to manage products, and delivery personnel should be able to update delivery status."

Clarification response for REQ-004: REQ-004: What pass/fail acceptance test, test data, and expected result will verify this requirement? Answer: "The system should allow customers to browse products, add products to their cart, complete payments, and track orders. Testing should verify that each operation completes successfully."

Clarification response for REQ-005: REQ-005: What pass/fail acceptance test, test data, and expected result will verify this requirement? Answer: "Verify that customer information is protected, passwords are securely stored, and payment transactions are processed through a secure payment mechanism."

options.name: Spiral
options.suitability: Best when risk analysis, prototypes, and repeated risk-reduction cycles are central.

options.name: DevSecOps
options.suitability: Best where iterative delivery is paired with automated security, assurance, and operational controls.

options.name: V-Shape
options.suitability: Best when each specification stage needs a linked verification and validation activity.

options.name: Incremental
options.suitability: Best when value can be divided into validated, independently testable increments.

options.name: Agileâ€“V-Model hybrid
options.suitability: Best where evolving delivery needs formal verification and validation gates for regulated scope.

options.name: Agile
options.suitability: Best for frequent feedback and evolving requirements, with planned governance for high-risk work.

options.name: Prototyping
options.suitability: Best for validating uncertain user needs, workflows, and interfaces before committing to a full build.

options.name: Waterfall
options.suitability: Best when requirements are stable, fully specified, and changes are controlled.

options.name: RAD
options.suitability: Best for time-boxed delivery with available users and modular, lower-risk scope.
